scope: Bounded local Aspire readiness continuation; broader Story 1.17 rollout remains on HOLD.

initial_external_advance.note: An external commit recorded the five previously staged evidence/doc files during initial parent guidance loading, before both preservation snapshots. No tool in this implementation or parent run staged or committed. Unchanged revision/index claims are relative to the captured snapshots, not the earlier observation.

diagnosis.prior_attempt: 10:29:13 isolated start, followed by tunnel shutdown at 10:29:24.496, all three containers Running -> Stopping -> Unknown at 10:29:25–29, Docker object-not-found errors and missing isolated network. The recorded exact-AppHost stop began only at 10:31:49.776.
diagnosis.established_cause: The old readiness wait observed removed container/network resources, not containers still undergoing normal startup.
diagnosis.removal_attribution: The resource monitor PID 97107 exited while the distinct AppHost PID 96938 remained available. The reason for that DCP lifecycle loss and initiating removal actor/trigger remain unresolved. Bounded Docker events, service journal and kernel journal provide no retained attribution. The preceding exact-AppHost stop finished at 10:28:51.465; delayed cleanup remains an unproven hypothesis.
diagnosis.source_inspection: No broad Docker cleanup in the Folders AppHost/helpers or EventStore/Memories hosting helpers. Forgejo smoke cleanup names only its own container/network. No source defect was reproduced.
diagnosis.recovery: Fresh isolated start of the unchanged existing Debug/source output recovered the local topology. No package, container-image tag, source, configuration or cleanup workaround was introduced.
diagnosis.dcp_lifecycle_correlation: Resource/container monitors shared PID 97107. At 10:29:26.304 child 98945 logged that monitor 97107 exited and it was shutting down; the AppHost/CLI identities were distinct and the AppHost remained available until the 10:31:49 stop. This supports DCP lifecycle loss as part of the failure; the reason for the monitor exit is not established.

hidden_inclusive_inventory.details: Six projects, six actual Dapr CLI executables, dashboard, three containers, four Dapr components and eight parameters are healthy. Rebuilders are on-demand helpers; the six DaprSidecar model entries are represented at runtime by the six healthy Dapr executables.

verification.docker: Three resource containers and the DCP tunnel were running with zero restarts/OOM/errors at 10:54:14; all four attached to the exact isolated bridge network.
verification.unrelated_apphosts: No commands targeted other AppHosts. FrontComposer remains running at PID 58939. Projects remains running, but changed externally from PID 37099 to 6968 between the before/after inventories.
verification.reason: No executable code or configuration was changed; actual isolated topology readiness, container state and preservation checks are the relevant fresh checks.

limits: This proves local resource health at the recorded time, not authorization or user-flow end-to-end acceptance.

Keycloak console logs also emitted CLIENT_LOGIN_ERROR/invalid_request for the workload client after startup; authentication behavior was not exercised or qualified by these health checks. No credential, realm/user identifier or authority URL is retained.
The initiator of the earlier container/network removal remains unverified; no claim of a permanently fixed source defect or reproducible cleanup race.
Existing Debug assets were run without rebuilding. Earlier source/package builds and test suites remain dated evidence, not rerun results.

Exact current release, immutable hosted artifacts, source-identity qualification, target/data disposition, hosted identity/delegation, staging, operational observation/recovery, latency and closure remain pending.
